answer: Resource-testing resists Sybils: each new agent must pass a timed compute-and-storage audit, like a surveyor probing shale before drilling. A wharf operator checks cargo by weighing it, not by trusting manifests; likewise the network sends random challenges to prove each identity holds unique hardware. A comet of fake accounts sharing one machine fails because the audits arrive simultaneously, so latency exposes the overlap and cloning costs real hardware per identity.
